title: Supporting students after KUCCPS placement — practical next steps
description: A practical guide for Kenyan senior school principals on supporting Grade 12 graduates after KUCCPS placement results are released — managing disappointment, celebrating success, and guiding next steps.
body:
The release of KUCCPS placement results is an emotionally significant moment for recently graduated students — a moment of celebration for some, and genuine disappointment for others whose placement did not match their expectations. Schools that extend their support beyond graduation, into this specific moment, help their alumni navigate it more successfully.

Why this moment deserves school attention

Students have technically left the school by the time placement results are released, which means many schools consider their responsibility ended. Schools that maintain even a brief point of continued support during this transition period help genuinely vulnerable young people navigate what can be a confusing and sometimes distressing process, at minimal ongoing cost to the school.

Helping students understand their options after placement

A student who receives a placement different from their preference, or no placement at all in the first round, often does not know what options remain available — revision of choices, subsequent placement rounds, alternative TVET pathways, or direct application routes. A brief guidance resource, shared with recent graduates when results are released, outlining these options concretely, prevents students from assuming their only option has closed when it has not.

Practical gesture: A simple WhatsApp message to your recent Grade 12 cohort when KUCCPS results are released — congratulating those placed, and specifically noting that the guidance counsellor remains available to discuss options for those who did not receive their preferred placement — costs almost nothing but provides genuine value at a vulnerable moment.

Managing disappointment constructively

A placement outcome that differs from a student's hope is not necessarily a closed door — many successful careers follow a path that did not match original plans. Guidance that helps a disappointed student see genuine alternative paths, rather than only commiserating with the disappointment, provides more lasting value during this moment.

Celebrating genuine success stories

Sharing positive placement outcomes — with permission — both celebrates the individual student's achievement and reinforces to current students that the school's guidance and preparation genuinely leads somewhere. This also feeds naturally into the alumni network relationship covered in our guide on building alumni connections.

Connecting students to available support beyond the school

For students facing genuine difficulty navigating the post-placement process — financial barriers to accepting a placement, confusion about next steps — connecting them to KUCCPS's own support channels, or to relevant government bursary and loan programmes (HELB), extends appropriate support without the school needing to solve problems beyond its own capacity.

Closing the loop with data

Tracking, even informally, what happens to your graduates after placement feeds directly into the alumni tracking practice that improves your school's career guidance over successive years, discussed in our guide on career guidance under CBE.
